land.text: 'His domain encompassed Bactria, the main center', and Sogdia, after Darius III was seized in mid-330 BC
Bactria and Sogdia, which Alexander took in the campaign that ended with Bessus's capture

successors.note: The macedonian-empire dossier has the gain of Bactria and Sogdia in 329.

capitals.name: Bactra (Balkh)
capitals.note: 'In autumn 330 BC, at Bactra, he took the throne name Artaxerxes V.'

rulers.name: Bessus (Artaxerxes V)
rulers.title: King of Kings (claimant)
rulers.note: Seized Darius III in mid-330; took the throne name in autumn 330 at Bactra; executed at Ecbatana, died summer 329 (infobox 329).

correction.text: Bactria, 'the main center', and Sogdia, where he fled across the Oxus

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row; the Achaemenid Empire shape of 331 holds the whole east). The page also places Aria, Arachosia-Drangiana, Parthia, Hyrcania and western India in his realm, but Hyrcania and Parthia were governed by Nabarzanes whom Bessus appointed; the macedonian-empire dossier has Alexander taking those satrapies in 330, so they are not drawn as Bessus's land. Bactria region 838 cells (212,000 km2) and Sogdia 813 cells (206,000 km2); no area on the page.

region.text: Bactria, the main centre of his domain

ledger.note: 330: Bessus is proclaimed Artaxerxes V at Bactra. 'Together they arrested Darius III in mid-330 BC'; 'Bessus declared himself King of Kings of the Achaemenid Empire, assuming the royal name of Artaxerxes V', in autumn 330 BC at Bactra.

330: the eastern Achaemenid satrapies follow Bessus. 'His domain encompassed Bactria, the main center' (the page also places Sogdia within it); the page gives no year for the extent, so the year is the proclamation's.

329: Alexander crosses the Hindu Kush and Bessus's troops disperse. The page gives no year for the pursuit ('Instead of making a stand, Bessus fled into Sogdia by crossing the Oxus'); 329 follows the macedonian-empire dossier's gain of Bactria and Sogdia.
329: Bessus is arrested by his Sogdian officers, Spitamenes among them, and handed over; 'He was finally sent to Ecbatana, where the Macedonians had him executed' (infobox 329, summer).
329: Bactria and Sogdia pass to Alexander. The page ends Bessus in 329; the macedonian-empire dossier dates the gain 329.

intersect.text: the Achaemenid 331 shape inside Afghanistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Pakistan, Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan: the land achaemenid-empire ledger 44 split to Bessus in 330
the -326 keyframe of this dossier (its Gedrosia cut does not reach the split land)

minus.text: Bactria and Sogdia (the gain above) and Gandhara and the Punjab (the gains of 326)

region.text: the rest of the eastern land split to Bessus in 330 (Aria, Drangiana, Arachosia and the Hindu Kush), outside Bactria and Sogdia, as far as macedonian-empire ledger 34 (the matching gain) draws it: within that dossier's -326 shape, without Gandhara and the Punjab (Cophen campaign of winter 327/326)

ledger.note: 329: the rest of the land Bessus held passes to Alexander. Alexander the Great page: 'Spitamenes, who held an undefined position in the satrapy of Sogdiana, betrayed Bessus to Ptolemy' (329 BC) and Bessus was executed; 'The campaign took Alexander through a number of satrapies in present-day Afghanistan and Central Asia' (Aria, Drangiana, Arachosia and Bactria among them, no years). The page dates no occupation of Aria, Drangiana or Arachosia, so the year is the fall of Bessus (bridged). Mirror of macedonian-empire ledger 34 (the gain of this land from bessus-artaxerxes-v, fx-23 refix), so that the two dossiers agree; the compiler already applies the gain, and this loss is skipped as its pair. Without a loss here the dossier passed on only Bactria and Sogdia (fx-37, handoff H33 from fx-23-refixed). Review fx-37: region narrowed to the exact region of macedonian-empire ledger 34 (2,400 cells); the earlier whole split land minus Bactria and Sogdia (3,410 cells) also passed Chorasmia (Karakalpakstan, Tashauz, Khorezm), the Balkan and Ahal edge and 135 cells of Gandhara and the Punjab to Alexander in 329, which the Alexander page does not support (Chorasmia not named; the Cophen campaign in Gandhara is 'the winter of 327/326 BC').
329: the last claimant of the Achaemenid throne dies. The page: infobox 'died 329 BC' at Ecbatana; the text, summer 329.

wars.name: Alexander's pursuit of Bessus
wars.outcome: Bessus fled across the Oxus into Sogdia; his Sogdian officers, including Spitamenes, arrested him and the Macedonians executed him at Ecbatana (329).
wars.note: The page does not date the pursuit.

certainty.note: No page gives boundaries; Bactria and Sogdia are the regions.

sources.title: Bessus
sources.note: Seizure of Darius (mid-330), proclamation at Bactra (autumn 330), domain, flight across the Oxus, execution 329.

sources.title: Alexander the Great
sources.note: Bessus betrayed by Spitamenes in 329 BC and the pursuit through Aria, Drangiana, Arachosia and Bactria; fx-37, handoff H33.

notes: One page (budget 1-2). The achaemenid-empire dossier records a split at 330 against this slug ('Bactria and the east'); this dossier narrows the land to Bactria and Sogdia because the macedonian-empire dossier already takes Hyrcania, Parthia, Aria, Sistan and Arachosia from the empire in 330 and Bactria and Sogdia in 329. The page: the wider realm 'also places Sogdia, Aria, Arachosia-Drangiana, Parthia, Hyrcania and western India within his realm' but with Hyrcania and Parthia under Nabarzanes. Months are not on the page beyond mid-330 and summer 329; none is recorded. The Sogdian revolt of Spitamenes (329-327) has no dossier.
